answer: Reputation is a decaying score that only fresh verifiable work refreshes: each completed task ships a signed, time-stamped attestation, and any score idle for one epoch halves. Agents like echo, umber, and onyx thus resist sybils because a clone inherits only the stale snapshot of a dormant identity, sinking toward zero while it sleeps. Flooding the network with copies buys nothing: each new identity must perform fresh, staked, escrowed work to earn trust, so cost per attack grows linearly while gain stays near zero.
